papers.title: Artificial intelligence in university physics education: a systematic review of empirical studies
papers.key_finding_zh: 综述纳入 11 项大学物理教育实证研究，发现 AI 的效果随任务与教学结构而变化；部分研究报告短期收益，也存在独立表现迁移和识别错误回答的局限。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 可用来定位“AI 支持下的表现”与“撤去 AI 后的独立能力”之间的研究缺口，并据其参考文献进一步追踪原始研究。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 先读纳入标准、研究特征表和局限，再精读涉及实验、仿真与独立迁移的原始研究。
papers.limitations_zh: 证据库小且异质，采用叙述综合；不能据此得出 AI 对所有大学物理教学普遍有效的结论。
papers.key_finding_en: This review included 11 empirical studies in university physics education. AI outcomes varied with the task and instructional structure: some studies reported short-term gains, alongside limitations in independent performance after AI support was removed and in identifying incorrect responses.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Use this review to locate the research gap between performance with AI support and independent capability after AI is withdrawn, then follow its references to the original studies.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Start with the inclusion criteria, study characteristics table, and limitations. Then read the original studies on laboratory work, simulations, and transfer to independent tasks closely.
papers.limitations_en: The evidence base is small and heterogeneous, and the review uses a narrative synthesis. It does not establish that AI is universally effective across university physics teaching.

papers.title: Comparing AI chatbot, tiered, and textual support in physics problem solving: Effects on cognitive load and affective-motivational outcomes
papers.key_finding_zh: 268 名九年级学生完成浮力任务。AI 聊天机器人和分层支架组的自报告内在与外在认知负荷低于文本支持组；AI 与分层支架组的情感动机差异未达统计显著。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 可作为 AI 支架与传统分层支架的对照设计参考；建议将认知负荷作为过程指标，并另设概念理解与撤去支架后的独立任务。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 全文读支架配置、随机分组和测量工具，特别注意结果指标实际测量了什么。
papers.limitations_zh: 研究主要测量短期自报告负荷和情感动机，不提供真实实验操作、长期学习或独立迁移优势的证据。
papers.key_finding_en: A total of 268 ninth-grade students completed buoyancy tasks. The AI chatbot and tiered-scaffolding groups reported lower intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load than the textual-support group. Differences in affective-motivational outcomes between the AI and tiered-scaffolding groups were not statistically significant.
papers.phd_relevance_en: This study can inform a comparison between AI scaffolding and traditional tiered scaffolding. Consider cognitive load as a process measure, alongside separate assessments of conceptual understanding and independent tasks after scaffolding is withdrawn.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the full descriptions of the support configurations, random assignment, and measurement instruments. Pay particular attention to what the outcome measures actually assess.
papers.limitations_en: The study mainly measures short-term, self-reported cognitive load and affective-motivational outcomes. It does not provide evidence of advantages in operating physical laboratory equipment, long-term learning, or independent transfer.

papers.title: Open- versus closed-response methods of measuring students’ reasoning: A case study using the Physics Measurement Questionnaire
papers.key_finding_zh: 在 Physics Measurement Questionnaire 的两类题目中，先写开放解释未改变后续选择题答案；开放与封闭回答之间的差异表明，两种格式提供的推理信息并不相同。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 你的实验能力评估可同时保留选择题与学生对测量、误差和数据比较的解释，避免把选对答案等同于能独立推理。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 优先读题目设计、开放回答编码和两种测量格式的一致性分析。
papers.limitations_zh: 这是特定课堂和两类测量题目的案例研究；不宜把结果推广为所有开放题或选择题的普遍规律。
papers.key_finding_en: For two types of items in the Physics Measurement Questionnaire, writing an open-ended explanation first did not change subsequent multiple-choice answers. Differences between open and closed responses indicate that the two formats reveal different information about students’ reasoning.
papers.phd_relevance_en: An assessment of experimental capability can retain both multiple-choice items and students’ explanations of measurement, error, and data comparison, avoiding the assumption that selecting the correct answer demonstrates independent reasoning.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Prioritize the item design, coding of open responses, and analysis of agreement between the two assessment formats.
papers.limitations_en: This is a case study of a particular classroom context and two types of measurement items. Its findings should not be generalized to all open-ended or multiple-choice questions.

papers.title: Leveraging generative artificial intelligence for simulation-based physics experiments: A new approach to virtual learning about the real world
papers.key_finding_zh: 电势实验比较真实仪器、预制仿真和 AI 生成仿真三种条件。两类仿真组的概念评估成绩高于真实仪器组；研究强调提示、修订和验证 AI 模型的学习机会。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 与真实实验、仿真和 AI 的三条件研究直接相关。可借鉴条件设计，再加入实际操作、故障诊断和撤去辅助后的迁移评估。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 优先读干预活动、概念评估、组间可比性与讨论；将评价指标逐项对应到你的研究问题。
papers.limitations_zh: 初步研究的概念成绩结果不等同于真实仪器操作能力提升，也不证明 AI 仿真优于预制仿真。
papers.key_finding_en: An electric-potential laboratory compared three conditions: physical equipment, a prebuilt simulation, and an AI-generated simulation. Both simulation groups scored higher on the conceptual assessment than the physical-equipment group. The study highlights learning opportunities in prompting, revising, and validating AI models.
papers.phd_relevance_en: This directly relates to a three-condition comparison of physical experiments, simulations, and AI. Adapt the condition design and add assessments of equipment operation, troubleshooting, and transfer after support is withdrawn.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Prioritize the intervention activities, conceptual assessment, comparability of the groups, and discussion. Map each assessment measure to the PhD research questions.
papers.limitations_en: The conceptual-score findings from this preliminary study do not demonstrate improved skill in operating physical equipment, nor do they establish that AI-generated simulations outperform prebuilt simulations.

papers.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
papers.source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.key_finding_zh: 高中数学随机实验区分 AI 辅助练习与无辅助考试。无护栏的 AI 能改善练习表现，却可能损害撤去工具后的学习表现；教学护栏减轻了这种负面影响。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 为区分“有辅助时完成任务”与“无辅助时独立表现”提供跨学科研究设计参考，可迁移为物理实验中的撤去支架评估。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 全文读无辅助考试设计与两种 AI 条件；重点记录护栏如何避免直接交出答案。
papers.limitations_zh: 这是数学教育的相邻证据，不是物理教育或真实实验技能研究；无辅助考试也不能代表所有形式的远迁移。
papers.key_finding_en: A randomized experiment in high-school mathematics distinguished AI-assisted practice from unassisted examinations. AI without guardrails improved practice performance but could harm learning performance after the tool was removed. Instructional guardrails reduced this negative effect.
papers.phd_relevance_en: This offers a cross-disciplinary design reference for distinguishing task completion with support from independent performance without support. The design can inform assessments after scaffolding is withdrawn in physics laboratory work.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the full descriptions of the unassisted examination design and the two AI conditions. Focus on how the guardrails prevent the AI from simply giving away answers.
papers.limitations_en: This is adjacent evidence from mathematics education, rather than a study of physics education or physical laboratory skills. An unassisted examination also does not represent every form of far transfer.

papers.title: AI tutoring outperforms in-class active learning: an RCT introducing a novel research-based design in an authentic educational setting
papers.key_finding_zh: 大学物理随机对照研究中，按教学最佳实践设计的 AI 导师在所研究课时内带来更高的即时学习成绩，并用时更少；学生报告更高的参与感和动机。
papers.phd_relevance_zh: 可参考其教学目标对齐和 AI 导师设计，并把即时概念成绩与真实实验操作及后续独立迁移分别评估。
papers.reading_recommendation_zh: 全文读导师提示、交叉条件安排、测验和讨论，明确时间与教学形式的差异。
papers.limitations_zh: 结果针对特定课程与设计好的导师；不能外推到任意聊天机器人，也没有直接证明长期保持或真实实验技能提升。
papers.key_finding_en: In a randomized controlled study of university physics, an AI tutor designed around instructional best practices produced higher immediate learning scores in the studied lessons and required less time. Students reported greater engagement and motivation.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Use its alignment with learning objectives and AI tutor design as references. Assess immediate conceptual scores separately from physical laboratory performance and subsequent independent transfer.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the full tutor prompts, crossover condition arrangements, assessments, and discussion. Clarify the differences in time spent and instructional format.
papers.limitations_en: The results concern a particular course and a carefully designed tutor. They cannot be generalized to arbitrary chatbots and do not directly establish long-term retention or improved physical laboratory skills.

papers.title: Evaluating GPT- and reasoning-based large language models on Physics Olympiad problems: Surpassing human performance and implications for educational assessment
papers.evidence_type: Comparative performance study (LLMs vs Olympiad participants)
papers.key_finding_en: On a set of German Physics Olympiad problems, both GPT-4o and the reasoning model o1 outperformed the human participants on average. Prompting technique made little difference for GPT-4o, while o1 almost always scored higher than both GPT-4o and the human benchmark. Beyond correctness, the authors describe characteristic strengths and weaknesses of the generated solutions.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A peer-reviewed reference point for comparing LLM solutions with human solutions on competition physics, and for discussing what correctness-based scoring misses about solution quality.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the problem selection, the scoring procedure and the qualitative analysis of solution strengths and limitations; these are the parts most reusable for a solution-quality coding scheme.
papers.limitations_en: Results depend on the specific problem set and on model versions that are quickly superseded. Scores measure final-solution correctness against a rubric, not how efficient or instructive a solution path is, and say nothing about student learning.

papers.title: Mastering Olympiad-Level Physics with Artificial Intelligence
papers.evidence_type: AI system evaluation (preprint, not peer reviewed)
papers.key_finding_en: The LOCA agent framework splits long physics reasoning into small, verifiable steps and refines them through an augment-and-review loop. On the 2025 Chinese Physics Olympiad (CPhO) theory exam it scored 313 of 320 points, above the top human competitor, and 28.6 of 30 on the IPhO 2025 exam.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Directly concerns AI performance on the Chinese Physics Olympiad, and its step-wise verification design offers a contrast to judging AI solutions by their final score alone.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the description of the step decomposition and review loop, and the CPhO scoring comparison with human contestants and baseline models.
papers.limitations_en: An unreviewed preprint from the system developers, evaluated on one year of each exam. A near-perfect score shows answer correctness under official marking; it does not show whether the solutions are concise, readable or pedagogically useful.

papers.title: HiPhO: How Far Are (M)LLMs from Humans in the Latest High School Physics Olympiad Benchmark?
papers.key_finding_en: HiPhO compiles 13 Olympiad exams from 2024–2025 and grades 30 models with the official marking schemes at answer and step level, then assigns medals using the official thresholds. Closed-source reasoning models reached gold on 6 to 12 of the exams, open-source multimodal models mostly stayed at or below bronze, and most models remained well short of full marks.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Shows how official marking schemes and medal thresholds can be used to place AI and human performance on the same scale, a useful contrast to rubric-only comparisons.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Skim the benchmark construction and the step-level grading procedure; the model leaderboard dates quickly.
papers.limitations_en: A machine-learning benchmark preprint. It ranks models by exam scores and does not study students, teaching or the quality of solution paths.

papers.title: Comparing teacher-centered and student-centered agents based on prompt engineering: Effects on learning performance, cognitive load, flow experience, and empathy perception in physics learning
papers.evidence_type: Comparative study of two prompt-engineered AI agents
papers.key_finding_en: Two instructional agents were built on the Coze platform with different system prompts: a teacher-centred agent giving authoritative, content-focused answers and a student-centred agent that attended to prior knowledge and gave adaptive, supportive guidance. Students using the student-centred agent showed higher learning performance, lower extraneous cognitive load, stronger germane engagement, more flow and higher perceived empathy.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Evidence that the design of a custom AI tutor's prompt, not only access to AI, changes learning and cognitive load. Relevant to comparing a general-purpose chatbot with a purpose-built tutor.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the two agent prompts and how they were operationalised, then the sample, assignment procedure and the learning-performance measure before relying on the effect sizes.
papers.limitations_en: Both conditions used AI, so the study compares prompt designs rather than AI against no AI. Sample size, assignment and study duration should be checked in the full text. Outcomes are immediate performance and self-reports, not independent transfer after AI support is removed.

papers.title: Prompt Matters: How Pedagogical Engineering Shapes Behavior and Engagement with AI Tutors
papers.key_finding_en: In a randomized online study (N = 125) on conservation of momentum, an AI tutor whose system prompt built in active learning, cognitive-load management and growth-mindset support produced more student–AI interaction, higher reported engagement and motivation, and less cognitive overload than a tutor with minimal instructional guidance. Both groups made substantial pre–post learning gains.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Separates the effect of tutor prompt design on engagement from its effect on learning gains, which matters when comparing a general chatbot with a custom physics tutor.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Compare the two system prompts, the interaction logs and the pre/post test; note which outcomes differed between conditions and which did not.
papers.limitations_en: Participants were recruited online through Prolific rather than from a physics class, and the task was a single short topic. Gains are immediate pre–post scores; engagement and overload are self-reported.

papers.title: aiPlato: A Novel AI Tutoring and Step-wise Feedback System for Physics Homework
papers.key_finding_en: In a large introductory physics course, an AI homework platform gave step-wise feedback on open-ended solutions across four optional extra-credit assignments. Students who used it more had higher final-exam scores (standardized difference about 0.81 after controlling for prior performance), and usage logs showed students relied mainly on iterative feedback rather than solution-revealing help.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A concrete design for AI support on physics homework that tries to preserve productive struggle, with interaction-log measures that could be adapted to an AI-tutored homework study.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the tool descriptions (step evaluation versus tutor chat), the engagement measures and how prior performance was controlled.
papers.limitations_en: An optional, self-selected pilot without random assignment, so the exam difference may reflect who chose to engage. It is a preprint, and the outcome is course exam performance rather than transfer to unfamiliar problems.

papers.title: Material-based contextualization in physics: Student preference for household objects versus laboratory equipment in a resonance demonstration
papers.key_finding_en: 288 secondary and college students watched a resonance demonstration with wine glasses and one with tuning forks, in counterbalanced order. 58.3% preferred the household version and 14.9% the laboratory version; the household version was rated higher for interest, novelty and everyday relevance, while clarity and self-reported support for understanding did not differ.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Supports the case for low-cost, everyday materials in physics teaching: engagement rose without a loss in perceived clarity.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the demonstration design, the seven survey items and the paired comparisons.
papers.limitations_en: A single phenomenon and affective self-report measures only; no conceptual test, experimental skill or longer-term outcome was assessed.

papers.title: Recitation tasks revamped? Students’ perceptions of smartphone-based experimental and programming tasks in introductory mechanics
papers.key_finding_en: Nine smartphone-based experimental tasks and three programming tasks were added to weekly homework in a first-year mechanics course. Across repeated short surveys (up to 188 students), the smartphone experiments were generally feasible at home and were perceived more favourably than the programming tasks, and comparably to standard recitation tasks.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Shows how low-cost experiments can move into homework, a model for take-home experimental tasks.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Skim the task list and the feasibility and goal-clarity survey items.
papers.limitations_en: Perception surveys only, at one university; no learning or skill outcomes were measured.

papers.title: Smartphone-based undergraduate physics labs: a comprehensive review of innovation, accessibility, and pedagogical impact
papers.key_finding_en: The review catalogues more than 200 smartphone-based lab activities across mechanics, optics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism and modern physics, sorted by topic, sensor type (sensor- versus camera-based) and instructional design, and discusses accessibility, device variability and curriculum integration.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A broad map of camera- and sensor-based low-cost experiments for locating where video tools and home-built apparatus already exist.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Use the activity tables as a reference; skim the sections on camera-based activities and implementation challenges.
papers.limitations_en: A narrative catalogue rather than a systematic review of learning effects; pedagogical claims rest on the cited studies. A 2025 arXiv version (2504.11363) is also available.

papers.title: From answer machine to collaborative partner: impact of structured generative AI training on scientific problem solving in STEM education
papers.key_finding_en: In an RCT (N = 95), students first answered the Conceptual Survey of Electricity and Magnetism alone and then revised their answers in conversation with the Doubao model. A short training grounded in self-regulated learning (how GenAI works, prompting strategies, how to catch and fix AI errors) raised AI-assisted revision performance (d = 0.81): trained students turned 69.3% of wrong answers into correct ones versus 41.3% in the control group, with comparable overall cognitive load.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Shows that how students are taught to use a general chatbot changes what they get from it, which bears directly on comparisons between general-purpose and purpose-built AI tutors.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the training protocol and the coding of revision strategies; the incorrect-to-correct revision measure is a reusable outcome for AI-supported homework.
papers.limitations_en: Outcomes are revision performance while AI is available, measured in one session on one survey; the study does not test independent performance after AI support is removed.

papers.title: Where free chatbots fail in school physics: an evaluation across 780 Uzbek-language textbook problems
papers.evidence_type: Evaluation of LLM performance on textbook problems
papers.key_finding_en: Free versions of ChatGPT (GPT-5 family) and DeepSeek (V3 family) solved 74.5% and 77.7% of 772 scoreable grade 7–10 textbook problems. Both failed on the same 119 problems (15.4%), clustered in identifiable sections and in demands such as textbook-specific value retrieval, unit tracking and multi-step quantitative reasoning.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A school-level counterpart to Olympiad studies: it locates where chatbot solutions break down rather than ranking models, and argues for teaching pupils where verification matters most.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the joint-failure analysis and the section-by-section recommendation table.
papers.limitations_en: Scoring is correctness against textbook answers in one language and curriculum; free chat interfaces change over time, and the study does not examine students using the chatbots.

papers.title: Can artificial intelligence solve school-level physics exam questions? A decade-based evaluation using Turkish university entrance exams
papers.evidence_type: Evaluation of LLM performance on exam questions
papers.key_finding_en: On 84 physics questions from Turkish university entrance exams (2016–2025), DeepSeek V3.1, Gemini 2.5 Flash and ChatGPT-5 reached 78.6%, 69.0% and 65.5% final-answer accuracy with a neutral student-style prompt; the differences were not statistically significant.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A national-exam benchmark that can be set alongside Olympiad-level results when discussing how reliable LLM physics solutions are.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Skim the question selection and scoring; the item-level failures are more informative than the totals.
papers.limitations_en: Only final-answer correctness on multiple-choice items was scored; 84 questions give wide confidence intervals and no analysis of reasoning quality.

papers.title: Student engagement patterns in conversational AI tutoring: evidence from physics problem-solving
papers.key_finding_en: Coding 318 problem-solving episodes from 18 undergraduates using an LLM tutor in thermodynamics (ICAP-based plus inductive coding) gave five interaction patterns. Task-focused (44.3%) and collaborative problem-solving (34.0%) dominated, 65.4% of interactions were brief exchanges without student-initiated questions, and dialogic engagement concentrated on the harder problems.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Offers an ICAP-based coding scheme for student–AI tutor dialogue that could be applied to chat logs from an AI-tutored homework study.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the coding framework and the pattern definitions, then the relation between pattern and task difficulty.
papers.limitations_en: A small sample in one advanced course; engagement patterns are descriptive and are not linked to learning outcomes.

papers.title: Using generative AI to support students’ interpretation of kinematics graphs: a classroom-based approach
papers.key_finding_en: In five workshops, secondary vocational students used generative AI to explain, compare and check their reasoning about kinematics graphs, under a teacher-guided routine in which AI explanations (including wrong ones) had to be tested against axes, units, slopes, areas and intervals. Mean scores rose descriptively from 2.91/13 to 5.50/13.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A practical routine for treating AI output as something to check rather than an answer to copy, adaptable to AI-supported physics homework.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the checking routine and the workshop tasks.
papers.limitations_en: One class, no comparison group, and pre/post item sets not validated as equivalent; the gains are descriptive only.

papers.title: Constrained vs. unconstrained free-fall and projectile-motion AI problem-to-simulation generation: a pilot study
papers.key_finding_en: For five Force Concept Inventory free-fall and projectile-motion questions, a constrained problem-to-simulation system met every applicable criterion of a technical and physics-accuracy rubric, while unconstrained AI-generated simulations varied widely and included a complete generation failure.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Relevant to AI-generated projectile-motion simulations: it argues for constraining generation before any classroom use.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Skim the rubric and the examples of unconstrained failures.
papers.limitations_en: Five questions and no students; the study evaluates simulation quality, not learning.

papers.title: Reforming thermal expansion experiments using vision-based measurement
papers.key_finding_en: Machine-vision sub-pixel tracking with synchronised temperature logging replaced manual optical alignment in a linear-expansion lab (about 2.7% relative error), cut equipment tuning from about 70% to under 10% of the session, and made thermal hysteresis directly observable. In a parallel-group study (N = 84), the vision-based group scored higher on lab-report data analysis (d = 0.67), core knowledge (d = 0.99) and understanding of hysteresis and non-equilibrium states (d = 1.41).
papers.phd_relevance_en: Closest recent example of camera-based measurement turning a static verification lab into continuous observation, with learning outcomes reported; a direct comparison point for video frame-stacking tools.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the measurement pipeline, the time-allocation data and the design of the controlled comparison.
papers.limitations_en: One university lab and a single topic; group assignment and test validity should be checked in the full text, and outcomes are course assessments rather than transfer to new experiments.

papers.title: Student-Selected Videos Together with Scaffolding Questions Improves Learning in a Physics Course
papers.source: Journal of Science Education and Technology
papers.key_finding_en: In an introductory college physics course (N = 103, intact lab sections), students who searched for their own online videos and answered association questions did better on quizzes and gained more on the Force Concept Inventory than a reading-and-exercises control. Exam effects were only indirect, depending on how much students engaged with the questions; working memory, GPA and motivation predicted most outcomes.
papers.phd_relevance_en: Evidence that self-directed homework resources help only when paired with scaffolding questions, a useful parallel for unstructured versus structured AI help at home.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the association-question design and the engagement analysis behind the exam result.
papers.limitations_en: Non-equivalent groups without random assignment; mixed results across outcome measures.

papers.title: Disrupting gendered task division without achieving equity of parity: A centrality-affective paradox from a design experiment in undergraduate physics labs
papers.evidence_type: Design experiment with observation and pre/post survey
papers.key_finding_en: Larger lab groups, weekly random grouping and rotating roles led women to take central and experimentalist roles more often. Yet matched pre/post E-CLASS results showed a significant decline in women’s attitudes toward experimental physics, with no change for men.
papers.phd_relevance_en: A reminder for inclusive lab design: changing who handles the equipment does not by itself produce equitable outcomes.
papers.reading_recommendation_en: Read the three design changes, the observation protocol and the E-CLASS comparison.
papers.limitations_en: One algebra-based course with a majority of women bioscience majors; the design changes were made together, so their separate effects cannot be isolated.
